children: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) stepped up their buying in Indian equities on Friday, November 20, with provisional data showing
net purchases of ₹10,308.42 crore
. This was their biggest single-day buying this week and marked the 15th consecutive trading session of net purchases.
Domestic institutional investors (DIIs), meanwhile, were net sellers for the day, offloading equities worth ₹4,859.80 crore, according to provisional data.
The latest purchases take
FIIs' net buying in Indian equities this week to ₹32,646.67 crore
across five trading sessions, according to NSE fund flow data.
FII buying gathers pace through the week
Foreign investors have steadily increased their purchases over the past five sessions, with Friday's buying marking a sharp step-up from Thursday's ₹7,411.41 crore.

The sustained buying marks a sharp reversal in foreign flows. After offloading more than $60 billion worth of Indian equities during the market's peak-to-trough sell-off, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have cumulatively bought
over $14 billion in the past 15 trading sessions.
The latest run has also set a record for cumulative purchases during a continuous stretch of net inflows, signalling a strong revival in overseas investor appetite for Indian equities.

The scale of the comeback has made India the biggest recipient of foreign equity inflows among emerging markets. According to Bloomberg data, Malaysia and the Philippines are the only other Asian markets to have attracted some foreign buying in November. Taiwan has seen the steepest outflows, followed by South Korea.

Adding to the positive sentiment, Goldman Sachs has upgraded Indian equities to Overweight and set a Nifty 50 target of 28,500 by the end of 2027. The global brokerage cited attractive valuations, improving corporate earnings and a stronger growth outlook.
The return of foreign capital has coincided with a strong rally in domestic equities. Indian benchmarks extended their
winning streak to a fourth consecutive week
, the longest in five months, as sustained buying in large-cap stocks lifted the
Nifty and Sensex to nine-month highs
. The Bank Nifty also scaled a fresh record.
The Nifty and Sensex gained around 2.5% each during the week, while the
Nifty Bank advanced nearly 6%
. Over the past four weeks, the Nifty has climbed more than 14%, marking its
biggest such gain in six years
. The Bank Nifty has risen close to 20% over the same period.
The rally has added substantially to investor wealth, with the combined market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies increasing by more than ₹40 lakh crore to around ₹514 lakh crore.

The rupee also extended its gains on Friday, closing at 92.67 against the US dollar compared with Thursday's close of 93.29. The currency had touched a seven-month high on Thursday. Continued foreign investor purchases and easing crude oil prices have supported the domestic currency.

title: FIIs pump in nearly ₹32,700 crore this week, extend buying streak to 15 sessions
